about: Open-source personal finance manager, self-hosted and privacy-first.

prs.title: CSV imports pick one date order for the whole file
prs.broken: With the date format on auto, each row was read on its own. A US bank file got some dates day-first and others month-first, so transactions landed in the wrong months.
prs.changed: The import now decides the date order once from the whole column, the same way bank files in the QIF format already worked.
prs.matters: US exports import with every date in the right month and no silent mistakes.

prs.title: Bank CSVs with a time next to the date import
prs.broken: CSV exports that put a time after each date, like Revolut statements, imported nothing and marked every row as a bad date.
prs.changed: The importer now reads the date part and ignores the time.
prs.matters: People can import their bank statements without editing them first.

prs.title: Old Quicken files import dates from 2000 to 2009
prs.broken: Quicken writes dates from 2000 to 2009 with a space before the year, so every transaction from that decade failed to import.
prs.changed: The importer now reads those dates, so 3/ 1' 8 becomes March 1, 2008.
prs.matters: Imported money history no longer has a ten-year hole.
